title: fix(agents): block repeated memory searches with unchanged hits
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agents repeating unchanged `memory_search` results without reaching a critical block when `tools.loopDetection.enabled` is true.

Closes #169042.

## User Impact

Repeated searches with the same arguments and ordered hits now reach the existing loop threshold. Changing hit content, order, ranges, warnings, or stable backend metadata still counts as progress. Delivered scores and diagnostics are unchanged; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing outcome-hash owner now excludes four per-call debug timings and each hit's time-decayed aggregate score. It preserves the remaining result metadata, including text/vector scores and provenance. Explicit error results and unstructured results keep full comparison, so new error text cannot be hidden by normalization.

Thanks @PatrickTrent for the detailed report and @ericcaiwx-star for the original fix. The contributor commits are preserved; current main was merged into the branch without rebasing.

Production: **+35/-0**; tests: **+113/-0**; docs: **+7/-0**. The added projection belongs to the existing hash owner, with no new state, config, or parallel mechanism. No obsolete nearby path could be removed to offset it without broadening the repair.

## Evidence

- **Failing regression on main:** all three timing/score-drift cases failed (same query, alternating queries, empty results); 66 other tests passed. Wall time: **9.59s**. The original contributor patch also exposed an explicit-error fallback failure, now fixed by keeping error text in the comparison.
- **Final tests:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **69 passed**, **21.29s wall** on the shared host. Outcome, batch-admission, and post-compaction siblings together: **95 passed**, **141.21s**, including compiled-worker preparation.
- **Real local-model baseline:** native Ollama `qwen3:4b`, 32K context, FTS-only Memory Core, direct tools, isolated state, and enabled loop detection through `pnpm openclaw --profile loop-detect agent --local`. Main `c55ca8ce465f73f52bc879dd5b33812914ebca8a` executed **27 identical searches in 480.363s**, with 27 distinct raw payloads but one stable ordered result. Warnings only; no critical block.
- **Real local-model after-proof:** the same model, tool arguments, memory data, and entry point completed **20 successful searches**, then **attempt 21 was blocked** with `deniedReason=tool-loop`, `detector=generic_repeat`, `count=20`. The model reported the block and ended normally; **122.041s**, CLI exit 0. The first candidate attempt voluntarily stopped after the warning at 10 repeats; the successful blocking probe clarified that repeated observations were intentional and asked the model to report an actual runtime block. No provider fixture or injected tool calls were used.
- **Long legitimate local turn:** native `qwen3:4b` completed 24 distinct memory lookups and returned the verified 24-row table without interruption. **105.540s**, CLI exit 0, `aborted=false`, normal stop. There were 25 calls: the first cold-index search reported a revision conflict, then its retry and all remaining searches succeeded. This transient indexing warning is retained in the evidence; no loop veto occurred.
- **Local checks:** full build passed (**9m11.2s**), independent Codex autoreview is **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**, all baseline ratchets and config docs passed, production and all 28 test-type graphs passed, and lint, dead-export, plugin inventory/boundary, schema, import-cycle, runtime-loader, and applicable auth/webhook guards passed. The initial lint failure was a missing pinned lint dependency in the gateway-only install; a full frozen install repaired the environment without source or lockfile changes.
- **Exact-head CI / ClawSweeper:** [CI run 38168891780](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38168891780) and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed on `1ca8fb58d7093442142ac79c9cea9f6507f9cd76`; `ci:no-fail-fast` was enabled. The 9 selected Node jobs used 1180 cumulative job-seconds (35–301s each, including setup and sibling tests). ClawSweeper reviewed the same head at 2026-10-11 19:46:57 UTC: **no findings; no Before merge items; ready for maintainer review**.

Scope: no threshold/default/watchdog changes for #132021 or #120415. The local CLI proof exercises the embedded loop, not the Gateway watchdog that emits “stopped making progress.” A Llama 3.2 attempt emitted tool-call JSON as text after one invalid call and is not counted as loop proof.
